MAJOR: `architect_review_check.py` except clause references `subprocess.TimeoutExpired`, but the diff does not add `import subprocess` to that module. If it was not already imported at module scope, the handler raises `NameError` at exception time — the very fail-closed path this change introduces becomes the crash site. Verify/force the import in the same change.

`precheck.py::_git()` is now fail-closed with a 30s timeout, but no caller in the shown diff handles `GitError`. Previously a broken/missing git degraded to an empty changed-file set (gate continued); now `precheck.py` will terminate with an unhandled traceback for developers on machines where git is slow, absent, or a worktree is broken (cf. the known BI-PF-1331 WinError 206 worktree issue in the same backlog). Fail-closed is correct, but the developer-facing path needs a deliberate, human-readable exit, mirroring what `architect_review_check.py` got.

The "one policy for every caller" claim is not yet true: only `architect_review.py` and `precheck.py` were migrated. Any remaining gate/evidence script that runs `subprocess.run(..., text=True)` (e.g. review_learnings, baseline generation, gate1_check) still decodes by locale, so the same class of Windows/Linux divergence and locale crashes can resurface outside Gate 2.5 — and existing committed baseline shas produced under locale decoding may no longer match, re-opening previously accepted items. Audit and migrate (or explicitly enumerate the residual scope) in this ticket.

SHA equality across OSes also depends on git's own output normalization, not just Python decoding: non-ASCII paths are C-quoted by git unless `core.quotepath=false`, and `errors="replace"` does not undo quoting, so `changed_files()` can still differ across machines/configs. If any sha input derives from path lists, force `-c core.quotepath=false` (and ideally `-c i18n.logOutputEncoding=utf-8`) inside the shared helper so the policy is enforced centrally rather than per-caller config luck.
MINOR: `GitError` propagates uncaught out of `architect_review.py`'s own CLI entrypoints (`_merge_base`, `_git_diff`, `changed_files`). The check script handles it; direct invocations of `architect_review.py` will traceback. Add the same friendly exit there for symmetry.

`architect_review._git_text` is a thin wrapper around the shared helper — good reuse — but the wrapper takes `timeout` positionally into `gitutil.git_text(args, cwd, timeout)`, a fragile signature; keyword-only `timeout` in the helper would protect against silent mis-binding as the helper gains parameters.

The U+FFFD warning is advisory only and prints for legitimately present U+FFFD content; consider restricting the heuristic (e.g. warn only when `errors` substitution is detected in path output) to avoid alert fatigue in real diffs.

Test module now injects `ROOT/scripts/dev` onto `sys.path` and imports `architect_review`, `architect_review_check`, `gitutil` at top level. This makes the test suite depend on sys.path ordering and on repo-local `config/` state read by `architect_review_check._cfg()`; a config drift will fail unrelated tests. Prefer a fixture that resolves config explicitly.
NIT: `sys.path.insert(0, _DEV_DIR)` in `precheck.py` puts a generic-named directory first on `sys.path`, enabling shadowing of stdlib/site modules (e.g. a future `gitutil.py` elsewhere, `paths.py`). Long-term, prefer package-relative imports over path injection for the shared helper.
`gitutil.py` is a very generic module name for a "shared policy" primitive; consider namespacing (e.g. `devkit.gitpolicy`) so the single source of truth is unmistakable as the gate surface grows.

Committed generated-artifact churn (BACKLOG-SUMMARY.md, documentation-index.html) is expected per repo convention, but the timestamp-only footer edits add review noise; ensure the generators run as part of the same precheck invocation rather than as separate hand-triggered steps.
